output.brief: Last week's 5xx rate (0.41%) is within the normal range for this service. Over the preceding 26 weeks the mean was 0.354% and the upper edge of the normal band was 0.482%. Earlier weeks reached 0.51%, 0.47% and 0.45%, and every one of those was investigated with no fault found. The burn-rate page did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). The dashboard count matches the raw logs. The apparent "new pods error twice as often" result is a rollout warm-up effect. New pods start with an empty cache and time out against the database. The same gap appears in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy, and it adds only 10–20 errors. Bookings were unchanged and there were no customer complaints. I don't think v4.18 or the replica move is shown to be at fault. I'm fairly confident, but I haven't ruled out a small real effect from the release, the replica move or partner-sync traffic. Recommended: don't roll back and don't move the replica. Do not mute the alerting, because that would remove the safeguard. Note the week at ops review and apply the standard check to the week of 2 Nov. If that week goes above 0.48%, investigate it as an incident.
